title: Cloud Development Environment
definition: The practice of using cloud-based tools and platforms for coding, development, testing, and other software engineering activities, as opposed to using a local machine.

difficulty_levels.beginner: Imagine you're a painter, but instead of using a physical paintbrush on a canvas, you use a digital painting tool on a cloud. This lets you work on your code from anywhere, and it's all stored safely in the cloud.
difficulty_levels.intermediate: Cloud development environments such as GitHub Codespaces and Docker allow for rapid, isolated, and consistent development. This separation between development and production environments can improve workflow and reduce bugs.
difficulty_levels.expert: Cloud development environments represent a shift towards a more distributed and resilient software development paradigm. They can also improve security and privacy by limiting the data exposed on a developer's local machine. However, they can introduce latency and require a stable internet connection.

extra_fields.insight: The separation of development and production environments using cloud tools can enhance workflow and reduce bugs, while also improving security and privacy.
